newsitem.title: INDIA: Renowned criminal ordered released from jail.
newsitem.headline: Renowned criminal ordered released from jail.

text.p: Notorious convict Charles Sobhraj on Monday was ordered released on bail after more than two decades in prison, and he said he would never revert to crime.
"There is no reason to detain him any further in jail," chief metropolitan magistrate Prem Kumar told a court in the Indian capital after Sobhraj provided a personal bond worth 30,000 rupees ($835).
Minutes after the release order, however, Sobhraj was re-arrested by police. "They have again arrested him because he did not have any valid documents," lawyer Amit Sharma said.

Dozens of police surrounded Sobhraj as he waited for a written order for his release. "I feel great, like I'm born again," Sobhraj told reporters. Hundreds of police stood guard outside the Tis Hazari courtroom complex.

Sobhraj, 52, was first arrested in India for holding up a hotel jewellery shop in 1971. He has since been charged with a long string of crimes including murder, serving time for some and winning acquittal in others.
He said he wanted to say a prayer while heading to the French embassy to obtain identity papers. Asked if he would revert to crime, Sobhraj said: "Never. Never ever."
